title: Minasseroke (Strong's Neck)
summary: Minasseroke is connected with Little Neck, now Strong's Neck, at Setauket. The neck lies between Conscience Bay and Setauket Harbor and is associated in local history with Setalcott presence and a place remembered as Indian Ground.
listing_image_alt: Strongs Neck Site Setauket, or Indian Ground Site_5I5A0316 WEB
why_this_matters: Recognized as the sacred residence of a Setalcott Sachem, Minasseroke contains funerary objects that underscore its deep spiritual importance to local Indigenous communities. Acknowledging the Native roots of such areas ensures that the foundational geography and enduring spiritual heritage of Long Island are not erased by later colonial land purchases.
history_content: Minasseroke is more than a label for a peninsula. The name points to a lived neck of land remembered for Native settlement, leadership, planting ground, and later colonial land transfers.
translation_content:
Recorded alternate forms include Minesuc and Min-asouke. An early berry-related interpretation was later reconsidered; the name may instead refer to corn land or maize land, drawing on the remembered Indian Ground on the neck.

Why Place Names Matter

“The stories that go with our place names are important to tourists, who want to learn about cultural connections. The stories can also point us to the resources or environment at those places and offer glimpses into important events of the past.”

— Ngā Pou Taunaha o Aotearoa New Zealand Geographic Board, Celebrating 100 years of place naming (2024), ‘Reflecting, commemorating and celebrating our unique identity through place names’ section
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: the pin is placed on modern Strong's Neck to represent the clearly identified peninsula between Conscience Bay and Setauket Harbor; it is not an exact boundary for the historic Indian Ground.
